mainEntity.name: How much does a Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engine replacement typically costs £1,500-£5,500 for a reconditioned unit supply-only, depending on whether it is the 2.4L or 3.3L variant. Supply and fit through our UK specialist network adds £600-£1,200 labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timing chain noise on Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engines is usually caused by tensioner wear allowing chain slack, typically appearing between 80,000-120,000 miles. Ignoring the rattle risks chain jump and catastrophic valve damage requiring full Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: Why do Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engines consume oil?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engines, particularly the 2.4L G4KE, can suffer from piston ring wear that allows oil to pass into the combustion chamber. Additionally, direct injection lacks fuel washing over intake valves, leading to severe carbon buildup that exacerbates oil consumption and rough idling.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engine is usually worth it if the chassis, suspension, and interior are in good condition. A rebuilt unit costs £2,500-£5,500 fitted, versus £10,000+ for a newer replacement SUV, saving budget-conscious Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol owners thousands.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A straightforward supply and fit replacement for a Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol typically takes 3 to 5 days at a specialist workshop. This allows time for the engine to be delivered, mounted, and thoroughly calibrated and tested.

historyTimeline.h2: Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 2.4-litre Theta II and 3.3-litre Lambda II GDI petrol engines provided smooth, refined power for the Hyundai Santa Fe, offering a quieter, more responsive alternative to the dominant CRDi diesels, particularly popular for family motorway use and towing.

milestones.description: G4KE (2.4L, 174hp) and G6DB (3.3L V6, 276hp) introduced in the DM generation Santa Fe, replacing older port-injected units with direct injection for improved efficiency and power delivery.
Mid-cycle facelift brought minor ECU calibration updates and cooling system refinements to address early GDI carbon buildup and oil consumption reports.
Production of these naturally aspirated GDI petrol variants ceased in the UK market as the subsequent TM generation shifted focus toward turbocharged and diesel powertrains.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h3: The Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engines are generally smooth and refined, but high-mileage examples are prone to specific GDI-related wear patterns, notably oil consumption and timing chain stretch. Every rebuilt Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol engine supplied through our network includes upgraded internal components specifically designed to address these original factory failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch & Tensioner Failure - Why the Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol (G4KE, G6DB, 2012-2018)
problems.rootCause: GDI engine oil degradation and tensioner wear lead to progressive chain slack. This causes a distinct rattling noise on cold start and, if ignored, can result in the chain skipping teeth, leading to catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain kit, tensioners, guides, and oil pump chain before failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught early (audible rattle but no running issues). Adds 40k-60k miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The only realistic option after catastrophic failure. Factory-spec or better reliability.

problems.recommendation: If your Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol exhibits cold-start rattle or mild oil consumption, preventative timing chain and PCV servicing is highly cost-effective. However, if the engine has developed a bottom-end knock, severe oil burning, or has seized, a full reconditioned replacement with upgraded piston rings and timing components is the most reliable long-term solution.

problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Carbon Buildup - Why the Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol Requires Attention
problems.affectedModels: Hyundai Santa Fe 2.4 / 3.3 GDI Petrol (G4KE, G6DB, 2012-2018)
problems.rootCause: Direct injection lacks fuel washing over intake valves, leading to severe carbon buildup. Additionally, the G4KE is known for piston ring wear that allows oil to pass into the combustion chamber, causing excessive consumption and potential bearing wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blasting for carbon removal, PCV valve replacement, and high-quality oil flush.
repairOptions.longevity: Effective for mild consumption and rough idle. Does not fix worn piston rings.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt long engine with upgraded piston rings, revised seals, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Mandatory if cylinders are scored or bottom-end knock is present due to oil starvation.
